$comment: Shared table for the hdf-to-xccdf Group/@id encoder. Go (xccdfGroupID) and TypeScript (xccdfGroupId) both read it. XCCDF types Group/@id as groupIdType: an NCName that must also match xccdf_[^_]+_group_.+ (xccdf_1.2.xsd:821). 'passthrough' marks a gid that already conforms and must be emitted unchanged.

cases.why: real STIG group id: already conforms, so it is preserved
reverse-DNS owner with dots is a legal NCName
real container-scan gid: bare STIG id fails the pattern
real SV-style id; underscores are legal inside the trailing name
real CIS-style gid: spaces are not NCName characters
empty owner segment does not satisfy xccdf_[^_]+_group_
an owner containing '_' does not satisfy [^_]+
the trailing name is required by .+
outside the ASCII set the check deliberately narrows to
matches the pattern but is not ASCII, so it is re-encoded rather than trusted
the pattern's .+ requires a trailing name; the converter skips empty gids, so this only keeps the encoder total
astral code point: one character, so one underscore — the TS regex needs the u flag to match Go's rune-wise Map

$commentRealShapes: realShapes: one representative gid per shape that reaches tags.gid. xccdf-results-to-hdf is the only converter that writes tags.gid (Group/@id verbatim); the other shapes arrive through InSpec profile passthrough (legacyhdf-to-hdf, splunk-to-hdf). Both languages assert the encoder leaves each untouched (passthrough, or prefix + gid verbatim), which is what makes encoding collision-free for real content without sampling it. Add a row when a converter starts emitting a new shape.
